findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: GetWebAssets reads entryPointAssetsCache under a read lock, releases it, and then acquires the write lock at line 48 — but never re-checks the cache once the write lock is held. When multiple requests race before the cache is first populated (e.g. at startup), each one sequentially re-opens and re-parses assets-manifest.json and overwrites the cache, defeating most of the benefit of the fix. Worse, if goroutine B populates the cache successfully and goroutine A's redundant re-read then fails (file removed during startup, transient I/O error), line 69 stores nil over the valid cache and A returns an error to its caller even though assets were already loaded. Add a second nil check after acquiring the write lock (standard double-checked locking) so only the first caller performs the load.

findings.title: Exclusive lock held across file (and potential network) I/O
findings.body: The write lock is taken at line 48 and held via defer for the entire remainder of GetWebAssets, which includes the assets-manifest.json read at line 60 and — if the cdn variable at line 54 is ever set to a non-empty value as the comment suggests — a CDN HTTP fetch via http.DefaultClient, which has no timeout. While one caller performs that I/O, every other goroutine calling GetWebAssets blocks on the mutex, including callers that would have been satisfied by the already-populated cache; in dev mode (where the cache is never consulted) this serializes every call. Consider performing the load outside the critical section and taking the write lock only to publish the result, combined with the double-check described above.

findings.title: No regression test for the data race being fixed
findings.body: This PR exists to fix a data race on the global entryPointAssetsCache, but it adds no test that would catch a regression. A test that invokes GetWebAssets concurrently from multiple goroutines (with cfg.Env != setting.Dev so the cache path is exercised) and is run under `go test -race` would fail before this change and pass after it. Without such a test, a future refactor of this function can silently reintroduce the unsynchronized access, and CI will not notice.
